key_insight: AmbiSuR identifies and addresses built-in primitive-wise photometric ambiguities in Gaussian Splatting, introducing an ambiguity-aware reconstruction pipeline that produces significantly more accurate surfaces from differentiable rendering.
problem_solved: Removes the photometric-ambiguity bottleneck that prevents accurate surface reconstruction from multi-view images when using Gaussian Splatting and differentiable rendering.
method: Analyze Gaussian Splatting representation and reveal two primitive-wise ambiguities that cause geometry–appearance degeneracy.
Introduce AmbiSuR: ambiguity-aware losses and per-primitive regularization to disentangle photometry from geometry within the splat optimization.
Pipeline: ambiguity-robust differentiable rendering + optimized splats → ambiguity-aware surface extraction to produce high-fidelity meshes.
impact: Makes Gaussian-Splatting-based reconstruction more robust and accurate under challenging photometric conditions, lowering manual tuning and improving downstream 3D tasks (e.g., inspection, AR/VR content).
visual_elements: Illustration of the two primitive-wise ambiguities (schematic showing color vs. opacity/geometry tradeoffs)
Pipeline flowchart: input images → AmbiSuR optimization (ambiguity-aware losses) → splat optimization → surface extraction
Before/after side-by-side reconstructions comparing standard Gaussian Splatting vs AmbiSuR
Bar/line chart of quantitative gains (e.g., Chamfer distance, normal error, PSNR) across benchmarks
paper_title: Revisiting Photometric Ambiguity for Accurate Gaussian-Splatting Surface Reconstruction
paper_authors: Jiahe Li, Jiawei Zhang, Xiao Bai, Jin Zheng, Xiaohan Yu
